advances: The reflected-collision argument in accepted fact d41b002f3091f5c4 has a macroscopic tail, not merely one possibly negligible midpoint with \(74\) representations. After deleting the \(73\) largest geometric-mean pair weights separately at every physical midpoint, the total remaining geometric-mean weight is strictly greater than \(37Q/300\). Every retained pair consequently has at least \(73\) distinct no-lighter reflected companions at the same midpoint. This does not turn the tail into a matching or into an additive contribution to any existing capacity.

proof:
For a nonempty family \(\mathcal P_m\), retain the notation of accepted fact d41b002f3091f5c4:
\[
 S_m:=\sum_{e=\{u,v\}\in\mathcal P_m}
 \sqrt{\tau_u\tau_v},
 \qquad
 M_m:=\max_{e=\{u,v\}\in\mathcal P_m}
 \sqrt{\tau_u\tau_v}.
\tag{10}
\]
The ordering (4) gives
\[
 S_m=\sum_{j=1}^{k_m}u_{m,j}^{\rm gm},
 \qquad
 M_m=u_{m,1}^{\rm gm}.
\tag{11}
\]

Suppose first that \(k_m\geq74\). By (5) and (11),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{74}(m)
 &=S_m-\sum_{j=1}^{73}u_{m,j}^{\rm gm}\\
 &\geq S_m-73M_m.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
If \(1\leq k_m\leq73\), then \(E_{74}(m)=0\), while
\[
 S_m=\sum_{j=1}^{k_m}u_{m,j}^{\rm gm}
 \leq k_mM_m\leq73M_m.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus (12) remains valid in this case. Empty families contribute zero to all sums and require no value of \(M_m\). Summing (12) over the nonempty families gives
\[
 E_{74}
 \geq
 \sum_m S_m-73\sum_m M_m.
\tag{14}
\]

The proof of accepted fact d41b002f3091f5c4 establishes the safe global estimates
\[
 \sum_mS_m>\frac{39104}{200}Q,
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_mM_m\leq\frac W4,
 \qquad
 W<\frac{803}{75}Q.
\tag{16}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sum_mM_m<\frac{803}{300}Q.
\tag{17}
\]
Substituting (15) and (17) into (14) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{74}
 &>
 \left(
  \frac{39104}{200}
  -73\frac{803}{300}
 \right)Q\\
 &=
 \left(
  \frac{117312}{600}
  -\frac{117238}{600}
 \right)Q\\
 &=\frac{74}{600}Q
 =\frac{37}{300}Q.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
This proves (7).

Finally, a pair contributes to (5) only when its index \(j\) is at least \(74\). The first \(73\) pairs in the ordering are distinct pair occurrences at the same midpoint, and (4) gives (9). This proves the no-lighter-companion assertion and completes the theorem.
